entries.style_notes: This original Fortcamp palette uses crisp open syllables, resonant liquid sounds and intermittent soft stops; no Earth star catalogue, species-wide titles, or invented translation claims. Names are shared regardless of game gender, with optional route or habitat bynames used only when fitting a character.

entries.style_notes: The D&D 2014 rules identify drow as an elf subrace and describe elven chosen adult names plus family names, without requiring Fortcamp to adopt any drow house or gender hierarchy. These newly authored names emphasize darker velvety consonants and clipped internal stresses; family names and trade bynames are optional Fortcamp variants.

entries.style_notes: Fauns use an original pastoral and lightly classical phonetic palette, with the D&D satyr listed as an analogue rather than the same species or a mandatory reveler. Household and landscape bynames are optional; a Faun need not be a bard, priest, or reveler to have a personal name.

entries.style_notes: D&D Tabaxi are a feline-humanoid analogue, but their name grammar was not accessible in the consulted public directory, and Fortcamp Catfolk are not presumed to be Tabaxi. This original pool combines compact personal names and optional meaningful family or descriptive bynames; a character can use only the given name.

entries.style_notes: This original fox-folklore palette favors clear mora-like rhythms alongside shorter names and rougher consonants, influenced by Japanese phonetics without claiming a single imported kitsune religion or lineage. Family and travel bynames are optional, and fox tails or apparent cunning do not justify a title or epithet.

source_limitations: Alien: No official naming tradition consulted for this Fortcamp-original species; the supplied style guide provides the basis.
Dark Elf: Official rules verify general elven adult/family structure and drow subrace, not this original phonetic palette or any Fortcamp drow hierarchy.

Faun: The official species directory establishes a D&D analogue but does not expose naming rules; the Fortcamp names and sound conventions here are original proposals.
